blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: With unlimited carry-over a plan's NPV rises. Run twice, the solver reports the same NPV but different carried amounts in each year. What does that mean?

options.text: Equally good carry-overs exist, so the cash rows must have a bug
options.says: Alternative optima are normal; nothing is wrong with the rows.

options.text: Equally good carry-overs exist, so report them only with a tie rule
options.says: Right: carry-over is a choice the model makes, and equally good choices exist.

options.text: One of the runs is wrong, since carried amounts are unique for a plan
options.says: The NPV is the same in both runs; only the carry amounts differ, and they need not be unique.

options.text: Both of the runs are wrong, since carry-over cannot add value
options.says: Carry-over can add value: it lets a tight year use an earlier year's leftovers.

origin.section: Carry-Over Is a Variable Linking Each Year to the Next

questions.stem: Adding a two-year spending cap to a plan with capped carry-over lowers the NPV below the plan with no carry-over at all. What should you conclude?

options.text: The cap costs more than the carry-over gives, which planners should see as a scenario
options.says: Right: each rule's cost shows only by solving; the result is a legitimate trade-off to report.

options.text: The cap is written wrong, since adding carry-over can never lower the NPV
options.says: Carry-over alone cannot lower it, but the cap is a new restriction that can.

options.text: The carry-over is written wrong, since its cash rows should have raised the NPV
options.says: The carry-over rows are fine; the window cap is what lowers the value.

options.text: The cap should be dropped, since a lower NPV is never acceptable
options.says: A cap from a rate case is a real rule; the model reports its cost, it does not overrule it.

origin.section: A Cap on Carry-Over and a Cap on a Window Are More Rows on the Same Expressions

questions.stem: A carry-over model with a 10% cap and a two-year spending cap reports INFEASIBLE, although planners have a valid plan. The cash rows are written spend + carry_out = budget + carry_in. What is wrong?

options.text: The equation forces most of each year's money to be carried, which the 10% cap forbids
options.says: The equation forces spending, not carrying; the cap limits what can be carried.

options.text: The equation forces most of each year's money to be spent, which the two-year cap forbids
options.says: Right: with carry-over capped, money that is neither spent nor carried must be allowed to lapse, so the row is an inequality.

options.text: The two-year cap is below the must-do spend, which no plan can meet
options.says: The planners' valid plan meets both caps, so the caps alone are satisfiable.

options.text: The 10% cap is below the leftover money, which no plan can meet
options.says: Leftovers above the cap can lapse in the world; only the equation forbids it.

origin.section: Unspent Money Lapses, So the Cash Row Is an Inequality
